Z2Z^{2}-Sampling: Zero-Cost Zigzag Trajectories for Semantic Alignment in Diffusion Models

Haosen Li∗, Affiliation: ∗Equal contribution. †Corresponding author: wchen179@connect.hkust-gz.edu.cn, yutaoyue@hkust-gz.edu.cn Affiliation: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)    Wenshuo Chen∗† Affiliation: ∗Equal contribution. †Corresponding author: wchen179@connect.hkust-gz.edu.cn, yutaoyue@hkust-gz.edu.cn Affiliation: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)    Shaofeng Liang Affiliation: ∗Equal contribution. †Corresponding author: wchen179@connect.hkust-gz.edu.cn, yutaoyue@hkust-gz.edu.cn Affiliation: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)    Lei Wang Affiliation: ∗Equal contribution. †Corresponding author: wchen179@connect.hkust-gz.edu.cn, yutaoyue@hkust-gz.edu.cn Affiliation: Griffith University & Data61/CSIRO    Kaishen Yuan Affiliation: ∗Equal contribution. †Corresponding author: wchen179@connect.hkust-gz.edu.cn, yutaoyue@hkust-gz.edu.cn Affiliation: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)    Yutao Yue† Affiliation: ∗Equal contribution. †Corresponding author: wchen179@connect.hkust-gz.edu.cn, yutaoyue@hkust-gz.edu.cn Affiliation: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
Abstract

Diffusion models have achieved unprecedented success in text-aligned generation, largely driven by Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG). However, standard CFG operates strictly on instantaneous gradients, omitting the intrinsic curvature of the data manifold. Recent methods like Zigzag-sampling (Z-Sampling) explicitly traverse multi-step forward-backward trajectories to probe this curvature, significantly improving semantic alignment. Yet, these explicit traversals triple the Neural Function Evaluation (NFE) cost and introduce unconstrained truncation errors from off-manifold evaluations, causing cumulative drift from the true marginal distribution.

In this paper, we theoretically demonstrate that the explicit zigzag sequence is topologically reducible. We propose Implicit Z-Sampling, rigorously proving that intermediate states can be algebraically annihilated via operator dualities, physically eliminating off-manifold approximation errors. To push sampling efficiency to its theoretical lower bound, we introduce Z2Z^{2}-Sampling (Zero-cost Zigzag Sampling). Exploiting the Probability Flow ODE’s temporal coherence, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling couples implicit algebraic collapse with a dynamically cached Temporal Semantic Surrogate. This restores the standard 2-NFE baseline without sacrificing semantic exploration. We formally prove via Backward Error Analysis that this discrete collapse inherently synthesizes a directional derivative curvature penalty. Finally, extensive evaluations demonstrate that Z2Z^{2}-Sampling structurally shatters the performance-efficiency Pareto frontier. We validate its universal applicability across diverse architectures (U-Nets, DiTs) and modalities (image/video), establishing seamless orthogonality with advanced alignment frameworks (AYS, Diffusion-DPO).

1 Introduction

Diffusion models [4, 5, 3, 52, 29, 13] have redefined the landscape of text-to-image  [9, 42, 41, 20, 22, 33, 31] and text-to-video [2, 23, 40, 10] generation. The cornerstone of this success is Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) [11], which steers the generative trajectory toward text-aligned data manifolds by extrapolating score estimates. However, standard CFG is “myopic”: it operates on the instantaneous gradient at the current latent state. Because the true data manifold of the Probability Flow ODE is highly non-linear [6, 15], localized linear extrapolation often struggles to foresee complex geometric shifts [21], leading to suboptimal alignment in dense compositional prompts.

To break this limitation, advanced sampling strategies, notably Zigzag Diffusion Sampling (Z-Sampling) [1] , oscillate the latent trajectory to probe local curvature [42]. By taking a forward step with a large guidance scale and a backward inversion step with a smaller scale, this lookahead-and-return mechanism [26, 49] accumulates semantic foresight [24, 25] and enhances structural coherence.

However, explicitly traversing the latent space introduces two limitations. First is the computational overhead: physical steps require sequential network queries, tripling inference costs per step. Second, explicit Z-Sampling [1] queries the network from an intermediate, uncorrected state. Because large guidance scales push this intermediate state off the true data manifold [6, 11, 15], evaluating the network at this out-of-distribution point introduces a persistent spatial error. This error accumulates over time, pushing latents away from the marginal distribution and causing numerical drift, structural artifacts, and color oversaturation [35, 19].

Can we leverage the semantic benefits of zigzag exploration without incurring computational overhead and off-manifold drift? Inspired by recent advances in direct ODE inversion [14]—which recycle latent noise to mitigate inversion errors during image editing—we address this question through the principle of Exact Noise Reuse. We propose Implicit Z-Sampling, which, instead of evaluating the network at out-of-distribution intermediate states, deliberately recycles the unconditional noise evaluated at the exact on-manifold anchor. Crucially, anchoring the inversion to this reused noise analytically cancels out the intermediate physical steps via the intrinsic properties of deterministic ODE solvers. This analytical simplification collapses the two-step oscillation into a single deterministic translation, strictly eliminating the off-manifold approximation error.

To maximize sampling efficiency, we introduce Z2Z^{2}-Sampling (Zero-cost Zigzag Sampling). While Implicit Z-Sampling eliminates spatial error, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling removes computational redundancy via temporal noise reuse. Leveraging the temporal coherence of continuous diffusion trajectories—a property widely exploited in multi-step ODE solvers [24, 55]—we design a dynamically cached Temporal Semantic Surrogate that decouples spatial curvature evaluation from the main integration step. Substituting exact spatial noise differences with this cached proxy restores the standard baseline of one CFG evaluation (2 NFEs) per step, preserving non-linear semantic exploration. Furthermore, via Backward Error Analysis (BEA) [8], we formally prove that Z2Z^{2}-Sampling synthesizes a modified Effective Vector Field. It naturally incorporates a directional derivative penalty that acts as a zero-cost geometric regularization, dynamically penalizing trajectory curvature.

Empirically, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling analytically eliminates off-manifold degradation, structurally breaking the conventional performance-efficiency trade-off. Evaluated at its absolute minimum time budget (∼\sim6s), it decisively outperforms the peak generation quality of explicit Z-Sampling (∼\sim18s). Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate its universal applicability across diverse architectures, from standard U-Nets (SDXL [31]) to Diffusion Transformers (Hunyuan-DiT [18]). Furthermore, it naturally extends to temporally coherent video synthesis (CogVideoX-2B [51], ModelScope-1.7B [44]) and establishes seamless orthogonal compatibility with both training-based (Diffusion-DPO [43]) and training-free (AYS [34]) alignment paradigms.

2 Preliminaries and Problem Formulation

First-Order Solvers & CFG. Deterministic solvers discretize the Probability Flow ODE into affine transitions. The forward step Φt\Phi^{t} and its exact inverse Ψt\Psi^{t} map the latent state via a prediction ϵθt​(𝒙t)\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t}):

Φt​(𝒙t,ϵ)\displaystyle\Phi^{t}(\bm{x}_{t};\bm{\epsilon}) ≜At​𝒙t+Bt​ϵ=𝒙t−1\displaystyle\triangleq A_{t}\bm{x}_{t}+B_{t}\bm{\epsilon}=\bm{x}_{t-1} (1)
Ψt​(𝒙t−1,ϵ)\displaystyle\Psi^{t}(\bm{x}_{t-1};\bm{\epsilon}) ≜At−1​𝒙t−1+Ct​ϵ=𝒙t\displaystyle\triangleq A_{t}^{-1}\bm{x}_{t-1}+C_{t}\bm{\epsilon}=\bm{x}_{t} (2)

This unified formulation is quite versatile, as it naturally recovers several standard sampler geometries depending on the choice of coefficients. For instance, in the standard DDIM [41] case (ϵ\bm{\epsilon}-prediction), we set At=αt−1/αtA_{t}=\sqrt{\alpha_{t-1}/\alpha_{t}} and Bt=1−αt−1−At​1−αtB_{t}=\sqrt{1-\alpha_{t-1}}-A_{t}\sqrt{1-\alpha_{t}}. If we opt for the Euler method in velocity prediction [20], the rule reduces to a much simpler form with At=1A_{t}=1 and Bt=σt−1−σtB_{t}=\sigma_{t-1}-\sigma_{t}. Furthermore, the framework extends to spherical geometries [16] (𝒗\bm{v}-prediction); by defining the angle as θt=arccos⁡(αt)\theta_{t}=\arccos(\sqrt{\alpha_{t}}), the coefficients become purely trigonometric, yielding At=cos⁡(Δ​θ)A_{t}=\cos(\Delta\theta) and Bt=sin⁡(Δ​θ)B_{t}=\sin(\Delta\theta).

Standard CFG [11] extrapolates locally via ϵθt​(𝒙t,γ)=ϵθt​(𝒙t,0)+γ​Δ​ϵθt​(𝒙t)\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma)=\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t},0)+\gamma\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t}), inherently ignoring manifold curvature.

Z-Sampling & Spatial Error. [1] Explicit Z-Sampling probes curvature via a lookahead-and-return path:

𝒙t−1\displaystyle\bm{x}_{t-1} =Φt​(𝒙t,ϵθt​(𝒙t,γ1))\displaystyle=\Phi^{t}\big(\bm{x}_{t};\;\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{1})\big) (3)
𝒙~t\displaystyle\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t} =Ψt​(𝒙t−1,ϵθt​(𝒙t−1,γ2))\displaystyle=\Psi^{t}\big(\bm{x}_{t-1};\;\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t-1},\gamma_{2})\big) (4)

While the original authors characterize an inherent inversion approximation error τ2​(t)\tau_{2}(t) within the score space, we identify a more fundamental geometric flaw. The large CFG forward step inherently pushes the intermediate state 𝒙t−1\bm{x}_{t-1} off the true data manifold. Physically evaluating the network at this out-of-distribution state diverges from the pristine on-manifold unconditional noise ϵθt​(𝒙t,γ2)\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{2}) (assuming γ2=0\gamma_{2}=0 for standard inversion). This divergence translates into a persistent spatial error τ⁡(t)\tau(t) upon inversion:

τ⁡(t)=Ψt​(𝒙t−1,ϵθt​(𝒙t−1,γ2))−Ψt​(𝒙t−1,ϵθt​(𝒙t,γ2))\tau(t)=\Psi^{t}\big(\bm{x}_{t-1};\;\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t-1},\gamma_{2})\big)-\Psi^{t}\big(\bm{x}_{t-1};\;\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{2})\big) (5)

Our Z2Z^{2}-Sampling annihilates this positional mismatch (τ⁡(t)≡0\tau(t)\equiv 0).

3 Methodology

Roadmap. We formalize our approach by: (1) Proving the algebraic collapse of spatial trajectories via exact noise reuse (Sec. 3.1); (2) Establishing Z2Z^{2}-Sampling by bounding the Local Truncation Error of our Temporal Semantic Surrogate (Sec. 3.2); and (3) Deriving the underlying Effective Vector Field to reveal the inherent continuous-time curvature penalty (Sec. 3.3).

3.1 Trajectory Collapse via Exact Noise Reuse

The fundamental flaw of explicit Z-Sampling lies in its spatial traversal: evaluating the inversion trajectory from the explicitly shifted intermediate state 𝒙t−1\bm{x}_{t-1} forces the network to operate off-manifold, injecting an unconstrained approximation error τ⁡(t)\tau(t).

To eradicate this deviation, we propose the principle of Exact Noise Reuse. Instead of moving to the uncharted state 𝒙t−1\bm{x}_{t-1} to estimate inversion noise, we recycle the pristine unconditional noise ϵθt​(𝒙t,γ2)\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{2}) evaluated at the on-manifold anchor 𝒙t\bm{x}_{t}. Anchoring the inversion to this reused noise circumvents the positional mismatch.

This deliberate algorithmic choice of noise reuse triggers an elegant mathematical consequence: the algebraic dualities of the ODE solver completely annihilate the intermediate physical traversal.

Let ϵθt​(𝒙,γ)≜ϵθt​(𝒙,0)+γ​Δ​ϵθt​(𝒙)\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x},\gamma)\triangleq\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x},0)+\gamma\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}) and logically set γ2=0\gamma_{2}=0.

Lemma 1.

Deterministic affine solvers satisfy algebraic dualities:

(i)​At−1​Bt≡−Ctand(ii)​At​Ct≡−Bt\text{(i)}\;\;A_{t}^{-1}B_{t}\equiv-C_{t}\quad\text{and}\quad\text{(ii)}\;\;A_{t}C_{t}\equiv-B_{t} (6)
Proof.

By definition, the exact inverse satisfies:

𝒙t\displaystyle\bm{x}_{t} ≡Ψt​(Φt​(𝒙t,ϵ),ϵ)=At−1​(At​𝒙t+Bt​ϵ)+Ct​ϵ\displaystyle\equiv\Psi^{t}\big(\Phi^{t}(\bm{x}_{t};\bm{\epsilon});\bm{\epsilon}\big)=A_{t}^{-1}\big(A_{t}\bm{x}_{t}+B_{t}\bm{\epsilon}\big)+C_{t}\bm{\epsilon}
=𝒙t+(At−1​Bt+Ct)​ϵ\displaystyle=\bm{x}_{t}+(A_{t}^{-1}B_{t}+C_{t})\bm{\epsilon} (7)

Since this holds ∀ϵ∈ℝd\forall\bm{\epsilon}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}, we get At−1​Bt+Ct=0⟹A_{t}^{-1}B_{t}+C_{t}=0\implies (i). Left-multiplying by AtA_{t} yields (ii). ∎

Remark 1.

This duality (Ct≡−At−1​BtC_{t}\equiv-A_{t}^{-1}B_{t}) is a topological constraint, unifying VP, Euler, and Spherical solvers without ad-hoc derivations.

Theorem 1.

Let ϵ1=ϵθt​(𝐱t,γ1)\bm{\epsilon}_{1}=\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{1}) be the forward guided noise, and let ϵ2\bm{\epsilon}_{2} strictly reuse the unconditional noise evaluated at the anchor: ϵ2≜ϵθt​(𝐱t,γ2)\bm{\epsilon}_{2}\triangleq\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{2}). Assuming γ2=0\gamma_{2}=0, under this exact noise reuse, the lookahead-and-return operator 𝒞t​(𝐱t)≜Ψt​(Φt​(𝐱t,ϵ1),ϵ2)\mathcal{C}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t})\triangleq\Psi^{t}\big(\Phi^{t}(\bm{x}_{t};\bm{\epsilon}_{1});\bm{\epsilon}_{2}\big) collapses into a deterministic single-step translation:

𝒙~t=𝒞t​(𝒙t)=𝒙t−Ct​γ1​Δ​ϵθt​(𝒙t)\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t}=\mathcal{C}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t})=\bm{x}_{t}-C_{t}\gamma_{1}\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t}) (8)

Consequently, spatial approximation error strictly vanishes (τ⁡(t)≡0\tau(t)\equiv 0).

Proof.

Expanding sequentially and invoking Lemma 1(i):

𝒙~t\displaystyle\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t} =At−1​(At​𝒙t+Bt​ϵ1)+Ct​ϵ2\displaystyle=A_{t}^{-1}\big(A_{t}\bm{x}_{t}+B_{t}\bm{\epsilon}_{1}\big)+C_{t}\bm{\epsilon}_{2}
=𝒙t+(At−1​Bt)​ϵ1+Ct​ϵ2=𝒙t−Ct​(ϵ1−ϵ2)\displaystyle=\bm{x}_{t}+(A_{t}^{-1}B_{t})\bm{\epsilon}_{1}+C_{t}\bm{\epsilon}_{2}=\bm{x}_{t}-C_{t}(\bm{\epsilon}_{1}-\bm{\epsilon}_{2})

Substituting ϵ1−ϵ2≡γ1​Δ​ϵθt​(𝒙t)\bm{\epsilon}_{1}-\bm{\epsilon}_{2}\equiv\gamma_{1}\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t}) completes the proof. ∎

Remark 2.

Physical Essence vs. Mathematical Form. Algebraic dualities act merely as mathematical vehicles. The zero spatial error (τ⁡(t)≡0\tau(t)\equiv 0) fundamentally stems from reusing the exact on-manifold noise. This renders the intermediate state 𝐱t−1\bm{x}_{t-1} a factored-out dummy variable, physically bypassing off-manifold errors rather than merely mitigating them.

Theorem 2.

The integration 𝐱t−1new=Φt​(𝐱~t,ϵ~t)\bm{x}_{t-1}^{\mathrm{new}}=\Phi^{t}(\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t};\tilde{\bm{\epsilon}}_{t}), where ϵ~t≜ϵθt​(𝐱~t,γ1)\tilde{\bm{\epsilon}}_{t}\triangleq\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t},\gamma_{1}), is isomorphic to a forward step initiated from 𝐱t\bm{x}_{t}:

𝒙t−1new=Φt​(𝒙t,ϵ~t+γ1​Δ​ϵθt​(𝒙t))\bm{x}_{t-1}^{\mathrm{new}}=\Phi^{t}\Big(\bm{x}_{t};\;\tilde{\bm{\epsilon}}_{t}+\gamma_{1}\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t})\Big) (9)
Proof.

Expanding Φt\Phi^{t} and substituting 𝒙~t\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t} from Theorem 1:

𝒙t−1new\displaystyle\bm{x}_{t-1}^{\mathrm{new}} =At​(𝒙t−Ct​γ1​Δ​ϵθt​(𝒙t))+Bt​ϵ~t\displaystyle=A_{t}\Big(\bm{x}_{t}-C_{t}\gamma_{1}\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t})\Big)+B_{t}\tilde{\bm{\epsilon}}_{t}
=At​𝒙t−(At​Ct)​γ1​Δ​ϵθt​(𝒙t)+Bt​ϵ~t\displaystyle=A_{t}\bm{x}_{t}-(A_{t}C_{t})\gamma_{1}\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t})+B_{t}\tilde{\bm{\epsilon}}_{t} (10)

By Lemma 1(ii), At​Ct=−BtA_{t}C_{t}=-B_{t}. Factoring out BtB_{t} yields:

𝒙t−1new\displaystyle\bm{x}_{t-1}^{\mathrm{new}} =At​𝒙t+Bt​(ϵ~t+γ1​Δ​ϵθt​(𝒙t))\displaystyle=A_{t}\bm{x}_{t}+B_{t}\Big(\tilde{\bm{\epsilon}}_{t}+\gamma_{1}\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t})\Big) (11)

∎

3.2 Temporal Surrogate and LTE Bounds

To avoid the overhead of querying 𝒙t\bm{x}_{t} while preserving zero spatial error (τ⁡(t)≡0\tau(t)\equiv 0, Theorem 1), Z2Z^{2}-Sampling caches a Temporal Semantic Surrogate to maintain the 2-NFE baseline (Algorithm 3):

Δ​ϵ≜Δ​ϵθt+1​(𝒙~t+1)≈Δ​ϵθt​(𝒙t)\Delta\bm{\epsilon}\triangleq\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t+1}(\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t+1})\approx\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t}) (12)

Exploiting rapid temporal stabilization (Figure 4), this surrogate uses a brief caching warmup to eliminate redundant queries, yielding a Local Truncation Error of Bt∼𝒪⁡(h)B_{t}\sim\mathcal{O}(h).

Assumption 1.

Let ℳ⊂𝒳\mathcal{M}\subset\mathcal{X} be the data manifold. The operator Δ​ϵθt​(𝐱)\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}) is uniformly Lipschitz continuous (Lx,Lt>0L_{x},L_{t}>0) strictly within a local neighborhood 𝒯δ​(ℳ)\mathcal{T}_{\delta}(\mathcal{M}). Beyond this, Lextruded≫LxL_{\mathrm{extruded}}\gg L_{x}.

Theorem 3.

Unlike explicit Z-Sampling which suffers an unconstrained 𝒪⁡(1)\mathcal{O}(1) persistent spatial bias off-manifold, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling bounds the surrogate error by 𝒪⁡(h)\mathcal{O}(h), yielding an 𝒪⁡(h2)\mathcal{O}(h^{2}) LTE and preserving convergence order.

Proof.

Explicit Z-Sampling: Let ϵθt​(𝒙t−1,γ2)≈ϵθt​(𝒙t,γ2)\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t-1},\gamma_{2})\approx\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{2})
𝒙t−1∉𝒯δ​(ℳ)\bm{x}_{t-1}\notin\mathcal{T}_{\delta}(\mathcal{M}). Since Lextruded→∞L_{\mathrm{extruded}}\to\infty, ‖τ⁡(t)‖\|\tau(t)\| injects an 𝒪⁡(1)\mathcal{O}(1) bias.

Z2Z^{2}-Sampling: The surrogate discrepancy is ℰTSS=‖Δ​ϵθt​(𝒙t)−Δ​ϵ‖\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{TSS}}=\|\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t})-\Delta\bm{\epsilon}\|. Invoking the Triangle Inequality within 𝒯δ​(ℳ)\mathcal{T}_{\delta}(\mathcal{M}):

ℰTSS\displaystyle\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{TSS}} ≤‖Δ​ϵθt​(𝒙t)−Δ​ϵθt+1​(𝒙t)‖+‖Δ​ϵθt+1​(𝒙t)−Δ​ϵθt+1​(𝒙~t+1)‖\displaystyle\leq\|\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t}(\bm{x}_{t})-\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t+1}(\bm{x}_{t})\|+\|\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t+1}(\bm{x}_{t})-\Delta\bm{\epsilon}_{\theta}^{t+1}(\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t+1})\|
≤Lt​h+Lx​‖𝒙t−𝒙~t+1‖\displaystyle\leq L_{t}h+L_{x}\|\bm{x}_{t}-\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t+1}\| (13)

Bounding the ODE step displacement by ‖𝒙t−𝒙~t+1‖≤K​h\|\bm{x}_{t}-\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t+1}\|\leq Kh yields ℰTSS=𝒪⁡(h)\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{TSS}}=\mathcal{O}(h). Modulated by Bt∼𝒪⁡(h)B_{t}\sim\mathcal{O}(h), the cumulative LTE is:

LTE=Bt⋅ℰTSS=𝒪⁡(h)⋅𝒪⁡(h)=𝒪⁡(h2)\mathrm{LTE}=B_{t}\cdot\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{TSS}}=\mathcal{O}(h)\cdot\mathcal{O}(h)=\mathcal{O}(h^{2}) (14)

∎

3.3 Backward Error Analysis

Applying Backward Error Analysis yields the Modified Equation.

Theorem 4.

For a CFG-guided ODE d​𝐱d​t=𝐯u​c​(𝐱)+γ1​Δ​𝐯​(𝐱)\frac{\mathrm{d}\bm{x}}{\mathrm{d}t}=\bm{v}_{uc}(\bm{x})+\gamma_{1}\Delta\bm{v}(\bm{x}), integrating the Z2Z^{2}-Sampling sequence solves a modified initial value problem governed by an Effective Vector Field:

𝒗eff​(𝒙)=𝒗u​c​(𝒙)+2​γ1​Δ​𝒗​(𝒙)−h​γ1​∇Δ​𝒗𝒗​(𝒙,γ1)+𝒪⁡(h2)\bm{v}_{\mathrm{eff}}(\bm{x})=\bm{v}_{uc}(\bm{x})+2\gamma_{1}\Delta\bm{v}(\bm{x})-h\gamma_{1}\nabla_{\Delta\bm{v}}\bm{v}(\bm{x},\gamma_{1})+\mathcal{O}(h^{2})

where ∇Δ​𝐯𝐯≜𝐉𝐯​Δ​𝐯\nabla_{\Delta\bm{v}}\bm{v}\triangleq\mathbf{J}_{\bm{v}}\Delta\bm{v} represents the Directional Derivative.

Proof.

Mapping to an explicit Euler discretization (At→1,Bt→−h,Ct→hA_{t}\to 1,B_{t}\to-h,C_{t}\to h), the intermediate state is 𝒙~t=𝒙t−h​γ1​Δ​𝒗​(𝒙t)\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t}=\bm{x}_{t}-h\gamma_{1}\Delta\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t}). Taylor expanding 𝒗~t≜𝒗⁡(𝒙~t,γ1)\tilde{\bm{v}}_{t}\triangleq\bm{v}(\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t},\gamma_{1}) around 𝒙t\bm{x}_{t}:

𝒗~t\displaystyle\tilde{\bm{v}}_{t} =𝒗⁡(𝒙t,γ1)−h​γ1​𝐉𝒗​(𝒙t,γ1)​Δ​𝒗​(𝒙t)+𝒪⁡(h2)\displaystyle=\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{1})-h\gamma_{1}\mathbf{J}_{\bm{v}}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{1})\Delta\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t})+\mathcal{O}(h^{2})
=𝒗⁡(𝒙t,γ1)−h​γ1​∇Δ​𝒗𝒗​(𝒙t,γ1)+𝒪⁡(h2)\displaystyle=\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{1})-h\gamma_{1}\nabla_{\Delta\bm{v}}\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{1})+\mathcal{O}(h^{2}) (15)

Remark 3.

Theorem 4 shows Z2Z^{2}-Sampling implicitly doubles guidance (2​γ12\gamma_{1}). While standard CFG collapses at ultra-high scales, explicit Z-Sampling survives due to a curvature penalty (−h​γ1​∇Δ​𝐯𝐯-h\gamma_{1}\nabla_{\Delta\bm{v}}\bm{v}) acting as a Riemannian centripetal force against off-manifold escapes. By algebraically internalizing this exact regularization, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling bypasses explicit Z-Sampling’s severe overhead and spatial drift, achieving zero extra cost and τ⁡(t)≡0\tau(t)\equiv 0 (shown in Appendix B).

4 Empirical Analysis

4.1 Experimental Settings

Datasets & Metrics We evaluate on three text-to-image (Pick-a-Pic [17], DrawBench [35], GenEval [7]) and one text-to-video (ChronoMagic-Bench-150 [53]) benchmarks. For images, we use HPS v2 [46], PickScore [17], ImageReward (IR) [47], and Aesthetic Score (AES) [38]. For videos, temporal consistency and prompt fidelity are measured via CHScore Flow [53], CLIP SIM [32], Frame LPIPS [54]/SSIM [28], and MTScore CLIP.

Models & Settings We test on standard U-Nets (SD-2.1 [33], SDXL [31], ModelScope-1.7B [44]) and DiTs (Hunyuan-DiT [18], CogVideoX-2B [51]), where we perform 50 denoising steps (T=50T=50). For the distilled DreamShaper-xl-v2-turbo [37], we set the denoising step TT only to 4 via the Euler sampler. We set the guidance scale γ1=5.5\gamma_{1}=5.5 for SD-2.1 and SDXL, γ1=6.0\gamma_{1}=6.0 for Hunyuan-DiT,

ModelScope-1.7B, and CogVideoX-2B, and γ1=3.5\gamma_{1}=3.5 for DreamShaper-xl-v2-turbo. The inversion guidance scale is set to γ2=0\gamma_{2}=0. Zigzag operations are applied strictly after stabilization, spanning the remaining λ=T−W−1\lambda=T-W-1 steps, where WW denotes the warmup duration. Specifically, we set W=5W=5 for standard image generation models, W=10W=10 for video generation models, and scale it down to a single step (W=1W=1) for distilled regimes (DreamShaper).

Baselines We compare Z2Z^{2}-Sampling against Standard sampling, AYS (training-free), Diffusion DPO (training-based), and Z-Sampling.

4.2 Text-to-Image Generation

Quantitative Analysis.

As shown in Table 1, standard CFG struggles with semantic alignment. While explicit Z-Sampling significantly improves prompt adherence, it triples inference latency (e.g., 5.8s to 17.8s for SDXL). In contrast, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling restores the standard 2-NFE baseline speed while matching or exceeding the semantic gains of Z-Sampling (e.g., achieving a PickScore of 21.88 on Pick-a-Pic vs. Z-Sampling’s 21.85). This empirically confirms that our implicit algebraic collapse captures manifold curvature without the redundant, expensive physical traversals.

Fine-Grained Compositional Generation.

On the GenEval benchmark (Table 3), Z2Z^{2}-Sampling achieves a superior overall accuracy of 57.35%. It particularly excels in complex relational tasks, outperforming explicit Z-Sampling in “Two object” (75.10% vs. 74.75%) and “Counting” (46.80% vs. 46.25%). This validates that our Temporal Semantic Surrogate successfully preserves non-linear semantic exploration while strictly avoiding the spatial off-manifold errors that typically cause object blending and attribute leakage.

Orthogonal Compatibility.

Table 2 demonstrates the plug-and-play versatility of Z2Z^{2}-Sampling. Integrating it into the training-free AYS framework yields compounded preference gains, boosting ImageReward to 103.90. Similarly, applying it to training-based Diffusion-DPO improves PickScore to 22.22 without adding inference latency. This proves that our implicit curvature penalty (∇Δ​𝒗𝒗\nabla_{\Delta\bm{v}}\bm{v}) is orthogonal to both step-distillation schedules and weight-level fine-tuning.

Qualitative Analysis.

Qualitatively (Figure 5), standard sampling omits elements in dense prompts. While explicit Z-Sampling improves semantic richness, its off-manifold evaluations induce a persistent numerical drift τ⁡(t)\tau(t), manifesting as structural artifacts and color oversaturation. By enforcing τ⁡(t)≡0\tau(t)\equiv 0 through exact noise reuse, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling fundamentally suppresses this degradation. It yields text-aligned, photorealistic images while bypassing the visual artifacts normally associated with high-scale guidance.

4.3 Extension to Text-to-Video Generation

The Spatiotemporal Bottleneck. Transitioning to video synthesis introduces the strict requirement of temporal consistency, rendering standard Z-Sampling infeasible. Its physical off-manifold traversals not only triple the inference time but also introduce severe numerical drift. When propagated across the temporal axis,

these spatial errors compound exponentially, aggressively destroying inter-frame continuity and leading to structural collapse.

Zero-Cost Generalization via Algebraic Collapse. In contrast, our proposed Z2Z^{2}-Sampling provides a seamless, zero-cost extension. By employing an algebraic formulation that physically bypasses off-manifold errors, temporal coherence is strictly preserved. Our cached Temporal Semantic Surrogate naturally adapts to spatiotemporal attention mechanisms without any architectural modifications. Evaluated on fundamentally different backbones (DiT-based CogVideoX-2B and U-Net-based ModelScope-1.7B), our method consistently outperforms standard baselines without introducing computational overhead (Table 4).

Quantitative and Qualitative Superiority. Empirically, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling stabilizes video generation. On ModelScope, it significantly boosts temporal consistency (CHScore Flow: 70.47 to 72.88; Frame SSIM: 79.13 to 81.03). On CogVideoX, enhanced perceptual continuity is confirmed by a reduction in Frame LPIPS (9.68 to 9.24). Qualitatively (Figure 6), while baselines struggle with high-frequency flickering (e.g., bamboo leaves) and disjointed rapid motions (e.g., branching lightning), Z2Z^{2}-Sampling locks in structural priors across the video tube. This enforces semantic alignment without accumulating numerical error, synthesizing videos with superior temporal smoothness and uncompromising prompt fidelity.

4.4 Ablation Studies

Effectiveness of the Temporal Warmup Phase.

To validate the necessity of stabilizing early generation trajectories, we ablate the temporal warmup mechanism in Z2Z^{2}-Sampling (Table 5). While applying Z2Z^{2}-Sampling naively from the initial noise state t=Tt=T already yields substantial gains over the standard baseline, it suffers from slight instability. This occurs because the initial denoising steps are highly chaotic, making the dynamically cached Temporal Semantic Surrogate less reliable. Introducing a brief warmup phase allows the continuous diffusion manifold to physically settle before caching the surrogate. As shown in Table 5, this simple temporal stabilization provides a strict performance boost across all benchmarks. Most notably, it significantly enhances metrics highly sensitive to early structural formation, such as ImageReward on DrawBench (77.38 →\to 80.12) and the strict Counting accuracy on GenEval (45.50% →\to 46.80%), confirming its vital role in preserving fine-grained geometric alignment.

Robustness to Zigzag Steps.

Figure 7(a) evaluates generation quality (win rate against standard sampling) versus active zigzag steps (λ\lambda). As λ\lambda increases from 0 (the baseline), quality improves monotonically across all variants, validating that non-linear probing effectively accumulates semantic information. Notably, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling consistently outperforms explicit Z-Sampling by strictly avoiding the accumulation of off-manifold approximation errors. Furthermore, the performance drop in the non-warmup variant corroborates our theoretical insight: early denoising steps are highly chaotic. A brief warmup phase prevents spatial estimation errors caused by forcing an early temporal surrogate, securing semantic gains.

Shattering the Performance-Efficiency Pareto Frontier.

Figure 7(b) illustrates the core empirical achievement of our method by evaluating text-image alignment (HPS v2) against inference time per image. In standard diffusion generation, explicit Z-Sampling (red curve) breaks the standard alignment ceiling but incurs a severe computational penalty, rendering its Pareto performance highly inefficient. Our Z2Z^{2}-Sampling (green curve) structurally shatters this conventional trade-off. By algebraically eliminating the off-manifold approximation error and reducing the computational cost back to the standard 2-NFE baseline via the Temporal Semantic Surrogate, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling strictly dominates the entire frontier. Remarkably, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling achieves a higher human preference score at its minimum time budget (∼\sim6s) than explicit Z-Sampling does at its peak computational allowance (∼\sim17s). This establishes Z2Z^{2}-Sampling as a zero-cost, high-yield semantic alignment paradigm.

5 Conclusion

In this paper, we introduced Z2Z^{2}-Sampling, a zero-cost paradigm that resolves the computational and geometric bottlenecks of explicit zigzag trajectories in diffusion models. By leveraging Exact Noise Reuse and ODE solver dualities, our method mathematically bypasses intermediate physical traversals, eliminating off-manifold approximation errors. Furthermore, we integrate a Temporal Semantic Surrogate to restore the standard 2-NFE baseline while synthesizing an implicit curvature penalty to prevent structural degradation under high guidance. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that Z2Z^{2}-Sampling shatters the performance-efficiency Pareto frontier, establishing itself as a compatible, drop-in replacement for standard CFG across diverse architectures and modalities.

Zero Memory Overhead Analysis.

To rigorously validate the spatial efficiency of our approach, we profile the peak VRAM consumption during SDXL inference. As reported in Table 7, the Standard

DDIM establishes a foundational memory footprint of 7.0137 GB. Explicit Z-Sampling increases this footprint to 7.0145 GB (a +0.82 MB overhead), primarily due to the instantiation of a dual-scheduler system and the accumulation of intermediate latent states during its multi-pass forward-backward operations.

In stark contrast, our proposed Z2Z^{2}-Sampling restricts the peak VRAM to 7.0140 GB. The empirical overhead introduced by dynamically caching the Temporal Semantic Surrogate (the momentum tensor) is merely 0.31 MB. This microscopic difference confirms our theoretical intuition: by mathematically annihilating the intermediate physical traversals and strictly bypassing the inversion scheduler, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling seamlessly absorbs the memory cost of the surrogate cache. Consequently, our method achieves strict zero-overhead in spatial complexity, confirming it as a highly practical, drop-in replacement that places no additional burden on consumer hardware.

Appendix C Related Works

C.1 Semantic Information in Latent Space

Recent works have demonstrated that the prior information embedded within the initial noise latent significantly impacts the quality and alignment of image generation [36, 48]. For instance, observations indicate that specific regions within random latents can trigger the generation of localized concepts [27], while other approaches propose Golden Noise [56] to leverage a semantic accumulation approach. Furthermore, studies have highlighted that even minor perturbations in the initial latent can lead to drastic shifts in the synthesized outputs of diffusion models [30]. Consequently, explicitly injecting semantic information—such as low-frequency wavelengths—into Gaussian noise has proven effective in enhancing image quality and prompt alignment [46]. Building upon these insights, our work investigates semantic information from a guidance perspective, implicitly integrating it into the sampling trajectory without the need for explicit reference data.

C.2 Sampling Strategies of Diffusion Models

To refine the diffusion sampling process, various strategies have been proposed. Early methods introduced Resampling [26], which involves injecting random noise and performing iterative back-and-forth steps at each timestep—a paradigm later adopted for video generation. Similarly, methods like IRFDS [50] employ a pretrained rectified flow model to provide a prior, optimizing the initial latent for image editing tasks. However, they overlook the structural importance of the inverted latent by simply applying random noise, thereby limiting prompt adherence. In the realm of structural consistency, approaches such as Tune-a-Video [45] incorporate a denoising-inversion paradigm; yet, their end-to-end approach remains suboptimal due to the neglect of the guidance gap. Other approaches address spatial inconsistencies by proposing adaptive guidance mechanisms based on semantic segmentation [39], but their reliance on attention-level interventions restricts adaptability and robustness. Constraint-based methods attempt to refine generation from a manifold perspective—such as substituting conditional noise with unconditional noise [6] or applying spherical Gaussian constraints—though these often yield marginal improvements or require external reference data.

Notably, Z-Sampling [1] has emerged as a powerful technique to capture data manifold curvature by explicitly traversing multi-step forward-backward trajectories in the latent space. While it significantly improves semantic alignment and transfers effectively to various generative paradigms, its explicit traversals introduce two critical bottlenecks: they triple the Neural Function Evaluation (NFE) cost per step and force network evaluations at intermediate, off-manifold states. This positional mismatch injects an unconstrained spatial approximation error (τ⁡(t)\tau(t)) that degrades generation quality. To resolve this fundamental flaw, we propose Z2Z^{2}-Sampling, a zero-cost paradigm that algebraically collapses the intermediate physical traversals. By coupling exact noise reuse with a dynamically cached Temporal Semantic Surrogate, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling strictly annihilates the off-manifold spatial drift (τ⁡(t)≡0\tau(t)\equiv 0) and restores the standard 2-NFE computational baseline. Consequently, it structurally shatters the performance-efficiency Pareto frontier, offering a robust, highly consistent semantic sampling trajectory without any computational overhead.

For continuous-time Flow Matching [20] and Rectified Flows, the trajectory is integrated via the explicit Euler method. The forward step is simply 𝒙t−1=𝒙t+(σt−1−σt)​𝒗θ\bm{x}_{t-1}=\bm{x}_{t}+(\sigma_{t-1}-\sigma_{t})\bm{v}_{\theta}:

𝒙t−1new=𝒙t−h⁡[𝒗u​c​(𝒙t)+2​γ1​Δ​𝒗​(𝒙t)−h​γ1​∇Δ​𝒗𝒗​(𝒙t,γ1)]+𝒪⁡(h3)\bm{x}_{t-1}^{\mathrm{new}}=\bm{x}_{t}-h\Big[\bm{v}_{uc}(\bm{x}_{t})+2\gamma_{1}\Delta\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t})-h\gamma_{1}\nabla_{\Delta\bm{v}}\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{1})\Big]+\mathcal{O}(h^{3}) (27)

Dividing by hh to express this discrete transition as a continuous-time differential equation yields the Effective Vector Field 𝒗eff\bm{v}_{\mathrm{eff}}:

𝒗eff​(𝒙)=𝒙t−𝒙t−1newh=𝒗u​c​(𝒙)+2​γ1​Δ​𝒗​(𝒙)−h​γ1​∇Δ​𝒗𝒗​(𝒙,γ1)+𝒪⁡(h2)\bm{v}_{\mathrm{eff}}(\bm{x})=\frac{\bm{x}_{t}-\bm{x}_{t-1}^{\mathrm{new}}}{h}=\bm{v}_{uc}(\bm{x})+2\gamma_{1}\Delta\bm{v}(\bm{x})-h\gamma_{1}\nabla_{\Delta\bm{v}}\bm{v}(\bm{x},\gamma_{1})+\mathcal{O}(h^{2})

By inherently synthesizing the penalty ℛ⁡(𝒙)=−h​γ1​∇Δ​𝒗𝒗​(𝒙,γ1)\mathcal{R}(\bm{x})=-h\gamma_{1}\nabla_{\Delta\bm{v}}\bm{v}(\bm{x},\gamma_{1}), Z2Z^{2}-Sampling projects the generative trajectory against the direction of steepest density descent, acting as a Riemannian centripetal force that dynamically bends the trajectory back onto the data manifold.

D.3 Annihilation of Spatial Drift

As emphasized in Remark 2, explicit Z-Sampling suffers from severe spatial drift. Here, we formally define this error and demonstrate how Exact Noise Reuse algebraically annihilates it.

The Emergence of τ⁡(t)\tau(t) in Explicit Z-Sampling

In the explicitly traversed zigzag path, the network moves to the forward state 𝒙t−1exp=𝒙t−h​𝒗​(𝒙t,γ1)\bm{x}_{t-1}^{\mathrm{exp}}=\bm{x}_{t}-h\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{1}). Because the CFG scale γ1\gamma_{1} is typically large, this explicitly constructed point falls strictly outside the high-density local manifold tube 𝒯δ​(ℳ)\mathcal{T}_{\delta}(\mathcal{M}). The physical inversion evaluates the unconditional field at this uncorrected off-manifold point:

𝒙~texp=𝒙t−1exp+h​𝒗u​c​(𝒙t−1exp)\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t}^{\mathrm{exp}}=\bm{x}_{t-1}^{\mathrm{exp}}+h\bm{v}_{uc}(\bm{x}_{t-1}^{\mathrm{exp}}) (28)

If we Taylor expand 𝒗u​c​(𝒙t−1exp)\bm{v}_{uc}(\bm{x}_{t-1}^{\mathrm{exp}}) around the on-manifold anchor 𝒙t\bm{x}_{t}:

𝒗u​c​(𝒙t−1exp)=𝒗u​c​(𝒙t)−h​𝐉𝒗u​c​(𝒙t)​𝒗​(𝒙t,γ1)+𝒪⁡(h2)\bm{v}_{uc}(\bm{x}_{t-1}^{\mathrm{exp}})=\bm{v}_{uc}(\bm{x}_{t})-h\mathbf{J}_{\bm{v}_{uc}}(\bm{x}_{t})\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{1})+\mathcal{O}(h^{2}) (29)

Substituting this back, we find:

𝒙~texp\displaystyle\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t}^{\mathrm{exp}} =𝒙t−h​𝒗​(𝒙t,γ1)+h⁡[𝒗u​c​(𝒙t)−h​𝐉𝒗u​c​(𝒙t)​𝒗​(𝒙t,γ1)]\displaystyle=\bm{x}_{t}-h\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{1})+h\Big[\bm{v}_{uc}(\bm{x}_{t})-h\mathbf{J}_{\bm{v}_{uc}}(\bm{x}_{t})\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{1})\Big]
=𝒙t−h​γ1​Δ​𝒗​(𝒙t)​−h2​𝐉𝒗u​c​(𝒙t)​𝒗​(𝒙t,γ1)⏟Spatial Approximation Error ​τ​(t)+𝒪⁡(h3)\displaystyle=\bm{x}_{t}-h\gamma_{1}\Delta\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t})\underbrace{-h^{2}\mathbf{J}_{\bm{v}_{uc}}(\bm{x}_{t})\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{1})}_{\text{Spatial Approximation Error }\tau(t)}+\mathcal{O}(h^{3}) (30)

The explicit traversal injects a continuous-time spatial drift τ⁡(t)≈−h2​𝐉𝒗u​c​(𝒙t)​𝒗​(𝒙t,γ1)\tau(t)\approx-h^{2}\mathbf{J}_{\bm{v}_{uc}}(\bm{x}_{t})\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t},\gamma_{1}). Critically, because 𝒙t−1exp\bm{x}_{t-1}^{\mathrm{exp}} is off-manifold, the Lipschitz constant bounds fail (as per Assumption 1), and the Jacobian norm ‖𝐉𝒗u​c‖\|\mathbf{J}_{\bm{v}_{uc}}\| becomes unconstrained. This introduces an irreversible numerical drift, manifesting visually as structural degradation and color oversaturation.

The Strict Annihilation (τ⁡(t)≡0\tau(t)\equiv 0) in Z2Z^{2}-Sampling

By enforcing Exact Noise Reuse, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling rigidly anchors the inversion step exactly at the on-manifold coordinate 𝒙t\bm{x}_{t}, reusing the pristine anchor 𝒗u​c​(𝒙t)\bm{v}_{uc}(\bm{x}_{t}). Consequently, the Taylor expansion entirely collapses:

𝒙~t=𝒙t−h​γ1​Δ​𝒗​(𝒙t)\tilde{\bm{x}}_{t}=\bm{x}_{t}-h\gamma_{1}\Delta\bm{v}(\bm{x}_{t}) (31)

Comparing this to the explicit case mathematically guarantees that τ⁡(t)\tau(t) is physically bypassed and strictly evaluates to zero (τ⁡(t)≡0\tau(t)\equiv 0). This ensures the complete elimination of off-manifold approximation errors while retaining the continuous-time curvature penalty.

Appendix E Failure Case Analysis

While Z2Z^{2}-Sampling structurally eliminates the off-manifold spatial drift τ⁡(t)\tau(t) and significantly mitigates the color oversaturation artifacts inherent in explicit Z-Sampling, it is not entirely immune to the stochastic challenges of diffusion manifolds. As illustrated in Figure 10, we identify two primary failure modes that warrant further investigation.

Surrogate-Induced Structural Inconsistency.

The first row of Figure 10 demonstrates that although Z2Z^{2}-Sampling produces a more natural color palette and sharper textures than explicit Z-Sampling, it may occasionally inherit or amplify structural errors. For instance, in the Mario case, Z2Z^{2}-Sampling results in an anatomical inconsistency (six fingers). This suggests that while the Temporal Semantic Surrogate error is theoretically bounded at 𝒪⁡(h2)\mathcal{O}(h^{2}), a rapid shift in the data manifold geometry during the zigzag phase can cause the cached Δ​ϵ\Delta\bm{\epsilon} to misguide fine-grained topological features.

Saturation Overflow in High-Density Priors.

The second row illustrates a ”saturation overflow” effect. In scenarios where the Standard Sampling baseline already achieves high semantic density and complex lighting (e.g., the Pope case), any further semantic enhancement—whether via Z or Z2Z^{2}-Sampling—inevitably pushes the latent state into the extreme extrapolation regime of the CFG field. In these instances, the enhanced semantic guidance becomes redundant, leading to oversaturation and loss of dynamic range, regardless of our method’s ability to eliminate spatial drift. This indicates that Z2Z^{2}-Sampling is most effective as a corrective mechanism for under-aligned prompts rather than a universal intensity booster.

Appendix H Overview of Evaluated Models, Datasets, and Metrics

In this section, we provide a comprehensive overview of the diffusion models, datasets, and evaluation metrics utilized throughout our empirical analysis to ensure self-containment and clarity.

H.1 Diffusion Models and Architectures

Our evaluations span a diverse set of fundamental architectures, including both standard U-Nets and recent Diffusion Transformers.

  • •

    Stable Diffusion 2.1 (SD-2.1) [33]: A foundational open-source latent diffusion model based on the U-Net architecture, trained on filtered subsets of the LAION dataset for high-resolution text-to-image synthesis.

  • •

    Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL) [31]: A significantly scaled-up successor to SD-2.1, featuring a massive U-Net backbone, a dual text-encoder system, and enhanced micro-conditioning mechanisms, allowing for superior compositional capability and photorealism.

  • •

    DreamShaper-xl-v2-turbo [37]: A highly optimized, distilled variant of SDXL (utilizing Adversarial Diffusion Distillation) designed to generate high-fidelity images in exceptionally few denoising steps (e.g., 4 steps), serving as our benchmark for ultra-fast sampling regimes.

  • •

    Hunyuan-DiT [18]: A state-of-the-art text-to-image model that replaces the traditional convolutional U-Net with a scalable Diffusion Transformer (DiT) architecture, demonstrating strong semantic adherence and Chinese-English bilingual comprehension.

  • •

    CogVideoX-2B [51]: A 2-billion parameter text-to-video generation model based on the DiT architecture. It excels in maintaining temporal coherence and understanding complex semantic motion prompts over continuous frames.

  • •

    ModelScope-1.7B [44]: A robust baseline for text-to-video synthesis utilizing a multi-stage spatiotemporal U-Net architecture to progressively generate and refine video sequences.

  • •

    Align Your Steps (AYS) [34]: A training-free sampling optimization framework that analytically determines the optimal timestep schedule for inference, which we combined with Z2Z^{2}-Sampling to demonstrate orthogonal compatibility.

  • •

    Diffusion-DPO [43]: A training-based alignment paradigm (Direct Preference Optimization applied to diffusion) that fine-tunes model weights based on human preference datasets.

H.2 Evaluation Datasets and Benchmarks

We measure semantic alignment and generation quality across several standardized, highly challenging benchmarks.

  • •

    Pick-a-Pic [17]: A large-scale, open-source dataset consisting of complex text prompts and crowdsourced human preference labels, heavily used to evaluate text-to-image alignment and overall visual appeal.

  • •

    DrawBench [35]: Introduced alongside Imagen, this benchmark comprises a curated set of challenging prompts designed specifically to probe the weaknesses of text-to-image models, including dense compositions, text rendering, and unusual spatial relations.

  • •

    GenEval [7]: An object-focused evaluation framework that rigorously tests fine-grained compositional capabilities. It isolates specific skills such as single/multiple object rendering, precise counting, spatial positioning, and color attribution.

  • •

    ChronoMagic-Bench-150 [53]: A specialized text-to-video benchmark focused on evaluating both prompt fidelity and the physical/temporal consistency of generated video sequences across diverse motion categories.

H.3 Evaluation Metrics

To provide a holistic assessment, we employ a suite of automated metrics targeting human preference, semantic alignment, and temporal consistency.

Text-to-Image Metrics:

  • •

    Human Preference Score v2 (HPS v2) [46]: A scoring model trained on a vast dataset of human choices to predict human preference regarding text-image alignment and aesthetic quality.

  • •

    PickScore [17]: A specialized metric trained directly on the Pick-a-Pic dataset, functioning as a highly accurate proxy for human visual preference in text-to-image generation.

  • •

    ImageReward (IR) [47]: A comprehensive reward model trained to align with human aesthetic values and strict text-prompt adherence, capturing nuances often missed by standard CLIP scores.

  • •

    Aesthetic Score (AES) [38]: A neural evaluator trained to predict the inherent visual appeal and artistic quality of an image, independent of strict text alignment.

Text-to-Video Metrics:

  • •

    CLIP SIM (CLIP Similarity) [32]: Measures the cosine similarity between the text prompt embedding and the visual embeddings of generated frames, quantifying semantic text-to-video alignment.

  • •

    CHScore Flow [53]: Evaluates the temporal consistency and logical motion progression of video sequences by analyzing optical flow dynamics across consecutive frames.

  • •

    Frame LPIPS [54]: Evaluates the temporal smoothness by computing the Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity between consecutive frames. Lower values indicate fewer abrupt perceptual shifts.

  • •

    Frame SSIM [28]: Computes the Structural Similarity Index Measure across adjacent frames. Higher values denote better preservation of structural elements over time.

Appendix I Limitations

Despite the significant performance-efficiency gains achieved by Z2Z^{2}-Sampling, this work has certain limitations that open avenues for future research:

Empirical Dependency of the Warmup Phase.

Z2Z^{2}-Sampling currently requires a brief warmup phase (WW) to stabilize the Temporal Semantic Surrogate. While empirical results suggest W=5W=5 for images and W=10W=10 for videos are generally optimal, these values are heuristically determined. The ideal duration may vary with specific noise schedules, manifold complexity, or total sampling steps. Thus, an adaptive mechanism to dynamically transition from standard CFG to Z2Z^{2}-Sampling based on trajectory curvature or signal-to-noise ratios remains unexplored.

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research.
